stories.deck_de: Die Kommission hat den Normungsauftrag M/606 am 10. Nov. 2026 geändert (C(2026)7861, M/606 Amd 1) und seinen Anhang I ersetzt: Nr. 1 und 15 vom 30.8.2026 auf den 30.11.2026, Nr. 16–41 vom 30.10.2026 auf den 31.1.2027; Nr. 2–14 unverändert (30.10.2027).
facts_de: Vorbehaltlich der Annahme durch die ESO

brief.en: The new deadlines are conditional. Art. 2: if CEN, Cenelec or ETSI “indicate that they do not accept the amendments … within a month of receiving it”, the Decision ceases to apply and C(2025)618 in its version of 3 February 2025 continues to apply. Harmonised standards developed under the request give a presumption of conformity once cited in the Official Journal; the deadlines bind the standardisation organisations, not manufacturers.
brief.de: Die neuen Fristen gelten unter Vorbehalt. Art. 2: Nimmt CEN, Cenelec oder ETSI „die Änderungen gemäß Artikel 1 des vorliegenden Beschlusses nicht innerhalb eines Monats nach seinem Erhalt an“, tritt der Beschluss außer Kraft und C(2025)618 in seiner Fassung vom 3. Februar 2025 gilt weiterhin. Harmonisierte Normen aus dem Auftrag begründen eine Konformitätsvermutung, sobald sie im Amtsblatt genannt sind; die Fristen binden die Normungsorganisationen, nicht die Hersteller.

stories.headline: Where ENISA consults: ten channels, two feeds, and drafts that are announced elsewhere
stories.deck: ENISA does not publish more than it did in 2023, but in more places and by more rules. Its certification work consults in an orderly way on its own website. Its guidance for manufacturers under the Cyber Resilience Act was put out for comment in 2026 as PDF files on its server, mostly without a news item on its site, and became known through LinkedIn and community mailing lists. The Cybersecurity Act 2 would make such guidance a standing task of ENISA, so far without a duty to consult on it.
stories.headline_de: Wo ENISA konsultiert: zehn Kanäle, zwei Feeds und Entwürfe, die anderswo angekündigt werden
stories.deck_de: ENISA veröffentlicht nicht mehr als 2023, aber an mehr Orten und nach mehr Regeln. Ihre Zertifizierung konsultiert geordnet auf einer eigenen Website. Ihre Leitfäden für Hersteller nach dem Cyber Resilience Act gingen 2026 als PDF-Dateien auf ihrem Server in die Konsultation, meist ohne Meldung auf ihrer Website, und wurden über LinkedIn und Mailinglisten der Community bekannt. Der Cybersecurity Act 2 würde solche Leitfäden zur Daueraufgabe der ENISA machen, bisher ohne Pflicht, dazu zu konsultieren.

stories.headline: Cybersecurity Act 2: debate in Parliament
stories.deck: The Irish Council Presidency (Marian Harkin) reported progress on the three main parts of the Cybersecurity Act revision (ENISA, certification, ICT supply chains) and aims for agreement in the Council by the end of 2026, so that trilogues can start in 2027.
stories.headline_de: CSA2: Aussprache im Parlament
stories.deck_de: The Irish Council Presidency (Marian Harkin) reported progress on the three main parts of the Cybersecurity Act revision (ENISA, certification, ICT supply chains) and aims for agreement in the Council by the end of 2026, so that trilogues can start in 2027.
facts: Speakers: Marian Harkin (President-in-Office of the Council), Henna Virkkunen (Executive Vice-President of the Commission)
facts_de: Rednerinnen und Redner: Marian Harkin (President-in-Office of the Council), Henna Virkkunen (Executive Vice-President of the Commission)

brief.en: Executive Vice-President Virkkunen put supply chain security at the core of the proposal, called for clear timelines to phase out high-risk suppliers, above all in 5G networks, and urged Parliament to give ENISA the mandate and resources it needs; she said full transposition and effective implementation of the NIS2 Directive could potentially have prevented some recent incidents or reduced their impact. Of the shadow rapporteurs, Tomas Tobé (EPP) asked for quick adoption with a framework to phase out high-risk suppliers, Jens Geier (S&D) for extending the scope to energy networks, and Markus Buchheit (ESN) opposed more resources for ENISA, a central reporting point and new certificates.

stories.headline: Chips Act 2.0: ITRE draft report

stories.headline_de: Chips-Gesetz 2.0: Berichtsentwurf im Parlament
stories.deck_de: Draft report of 9 November 2026 by the rapporteur of the Industry, Research and Energy committee on the Chips Act 2.0 proposal, with 226 amendments covering the whole proposal; it is the rapporteur's draft, not the position of the committee or of Parliament, and not law.

brief.en: It would shorten the permit-granting procedure to six months (extendable once by three months) and extend it to other publicly supported projects in the value chain, add first-buyer commitments for public buyers, an independent Semiconductor Expert Panel for strategic projects, competitive calls for European Semiconductor Regions and a European Semiconductor Strategy, and make the supply chain platform optional and participation in it voluntary. In the domestic-undertaking test it adds as domestic an undertaking holding a valid recognition under the Chips Acts, an IPCEI or another Union programme without a disqualifying change of ownership or control; in public procurement it adds a Commission template for the security of supply declaration, and for risk-prone sectors it requires evidence of significant supply chain risks and makes the dual-sourcing guidance conditional on an economically and technically viable alternative.

stories.headline: The ECCC: EUR 730 million in cybersecurity grants, paid out slowly, and a mandate that ends in 2029
stories.deck: The European Cybersecurity Competence Centre in Bucharest now manages 224 projects worth EUR 730 million from Digital Europe and Horizon Europe. Its budget peaked in 2024 and falls to about EUR 170 million a year; payments lag behind commitments by more than two years' worth. What comes after 2027 is open: Digital Europe is to merge into a Competitiveness Fund, and the Centre itself is set up only until the end of 2029.
stories.headline_de: Das ECCC: 730 Mio. EUR Fördermittel für Cybersicherheit, langsam ausgezahlt, und ein Mandat, das 2029 endet
stories.deck_de: Das Europäische Kompetenzzentrum für Cybersicherheit in Bukarest betreut inzwischen 224 Projekte über 730 Mio. EUR aus Digitales Europa und Horizont Europa. Sein Haushalt erreichte 2024 den Höchststand und sinkt auf rund 170 Mio. EUR im Jahr; die Zahlungen hinken den Mittelbindungen um mehr als zwei Jahresraten hinterher. Offen ist, was nach 2027 kommt: Digitales Europa soll in einem Wettbewerbsfähigkeitsfonds aufgehen, und das Zentrum selbst ist nur bis Ende 2029 errichtet.

stories.headline: Is ENISA equipped for its tasks? Half its money is temporary, and the Cybersecurity Act 2 would mainly make it permanent
stories.deck: ENISA's own budget has grown little since 2022 while the acts giving it tasks multiplied. The growth came from time-limited agreements with the Commission: in 2025 they paid 51 % of its revenue, and they run out in 2028. The Commission's proposal for a Cybersecurity Act 2 would turn much of that money into a permanent budget, but adds little on top, and its timing, the next EU budget and the fees are open.
stories.headline_de: Ist ENISA für ihre Aufgaben gerüstet? Die Hälfte ihres Geldes ist befristet, und der Cybersecurity Act 2 würde es vor allem verstetigen
stories.deck_de: ENISAs eigener Haushalt ist seit 2022 kaum gewachsen, während die Rechtsakte ihr Aufgabe um Aufgabe übertrugen. Das Wachstum kam aus befristeten Vereinbarungen mit der Kommission: 2025 trugen sie 51 % der Einnahmen, und sie laufen 2028 aus. Der Vorschlag der Kommission für einen Cybersecurity Act 2 würde viel davon in einen festen Haushalt überführen, legt aber wenig obenauf; Zeitpunkt, nächster EU-Haushalt und Gebühren sind offen.

stories.headline_de: CADA: neuer Schritt im Verfahren
stories.deck_de: Progress report of the Irish Presidency of 13 November 2026 on the proposed Cloud and AI Development Act, for Coreper to take note of and to pass to the Telecommunications Council of 1 December 2026; it is not a Council position and contains no legal text.

brief.en: It reports a first, partial Presidency compromise text on the autonomy part (the cloud sovereignty framework, public procurement and the public sector cloud federation), discussed in the working party on 10 November 2026: among other things, the Commission's implementing acts on Member States' assurance levels give way to recommendations, the mandated migration period goes from 12 to 18 months, the annual review of audit opinions becomes biennial, and the procurement rules extend to utilities' contracting entities. For the research and data centre parts, still being drafted, it announces among other things a later date of application (18 instead of 12 months after entry into force) and longer deadlines for data centre acceleration zones; the recognition architecture, penalties for SMEs and alignment with the proposed Cybersecurity Act revision and Public Procurement Act remain open.

For the research and data centre parts, still being drafted, it announces among other things a later date of application (18 instead of 12 months after entry into force) and longer deadlines for data centre acceleration zones; the recognition architecture, penalties for SMEs and alignment with the proposed Cybersecurity Act revision and Public Procurement Act remain open.

stories.headline: EU Space Act: Council working party meeting
stories.deck: Progress report on the EU Space Act of 13 November 2026, sent by the General Secretariat of the Council to Coreper and the Council for the Competitiveness Council of 3-4 December 2026, which are invited to take note of it; it records the work of the Irish Presidency, is not a Council position and changes no text.
stories.headline_de: EU-Weltraumgesetz: Sitzung einer Ratsarbeitsgruppe
stories.deck_de: Progress report on the EU Space Act of 13 November 2026, sent by the General Secretariat of the Council to Coreper and the Council for the Competitiveness Council of 3-4 December 2026, which are invited to take note of it; it records the work of the Irish Presidency, is not a Council position and changes no text.

brief.en: It reports on the Presidency compromise text of 29 October 2026: "EUSA verification" replaces "EUSA registration" for third-country operators and international organisations, the scope excludes space objects operated by military or defence authorities for their entire lifetime or owned by military authorities, a self-certification without a qualified technical body is offered for spacecraft with governmental ownership or operation, the rules on space-based data now centre on Earth observation data bought by public contracting authorities and Union bodies, and the environmental footprint gives way to a life-cycle assessment with a voluntary Union method. On cybersecurity the Presidency did not modify the provisions; the report says the compromise text deals with the scope of the NIS-2 Directive, third-country operators and derogations through two implementing acts. All Member States keep a scrutiny reservation, and the Working Party continues with a view to reaching the Council's position.
brief.de: It reports on the Presidency compromise text of 29 October 2026: "EUSA verification" replaces "EUSA registration" for third-country operators and international organisations, the scope excludes space objects operated by military or defence authorities for their entire lifetime or owned by military authorities, a self-certification without a qualified technical body is offered for spacecraft with governmental ownership or operation, the rules on space-based data now centre on Earth observation data bought by public contracting authorities and Union bodies, and the environmental footprint gives way to a life-cycle assessment with a voluntary Union method. On cybersecurity the Presidency did not modify the provisions; the report says the compromise text deals with the scope of the NIS-2 Directive, third-country operators and derogations through two implementing acts. All Member States keep a scrutiny reservation, and the Working Party continues with a view to reaching the Council's position.
